steps.prompt: Think of a time you tried to convince someone, a time you explained how something works, and a time you told a story about yourself. Which was easiest? Why?

cards.title: Argumentative: convince
cards.body: An argumentative essay takes a side and proves it with reasons and evidence. Its thesis is a claim someone could disagree with: “Schools should ban junk food because…”. Key words: should, must, better, because.

cards.title: Informative: explain
cards.body: An informative essay teaches the reader about a topic without taking a side. Its thesis names the topic and the parts you will explain: “Plastic harms the ocean in three main ways.” Key words: how, why, ways, causes, effects, steps.

cards.title: Narrative: tell a true story with a point
cards.body: A narrative essay tells a real experience in order: beginning, turning point, end. Its focus says what the experience meant: “The day I got lost at the fair taught me to stay calm.” Key words: taught me, learned, realized, changed.

cards.title: Same topic, two purposes
cards.telling: Students should learn to cook because it keeps them healthy, saves money and builds independence.
cards.showing: Learning to cook takes three skills: planning a meal, using a knife safely and following a recipe.
cards.note: The first argues (should… because). The second explains (three skills).

prompts: Which kind of essay do you most like to read? Which do you most like to write?
How can you tell an argumentative thesis from an informative one?
